item.title: Cape Zanpa — Guide
item.description: Cape Zanpa (Zanpa-misaki), on the west coast of Okinawa’s main island in Yomitan Village, is a striking headland where rugged coral limestone cliffs drop about 30 metres to the crashing sea. At its tip stands a tall white lighthouse — one of the few in Okinawa you can climb — offering panoramic views over the East China Sea and the wild, wave-battered coastline from the top. The cape’s raw, windswept scenery, with its jagged rocks, blowholes and open horizon, is a dramatic contrast to Okinawa’s calm beaches, and it’s a renowned spot for watching the sun sink into the ocean.

item.title: Lake Nakaumi and Yonago: Water, Birds and Sunsets — Guide
item.description: Lake Nakaumi is a vast brackish lagoon straddling the border of Tottori and Shimane, spreading beside the city of Yonago in western Tottori. Neither quite sea nor lake, its shallow waters are a haven for waterbirds — swans and countless migratory species winter here, making it one of the region’s great birdwatching spots — and its wide, open horizon delivers some of the most celebrated sunsets in the San’in region. Around it lie waterside parks, an island linked by bridge, and views across to Mount Daisen rising beyond.

item.title: The Seto Inland Sea Island Landscape — Guide
item.description: The Seto Inland Sea (Setouchi) is one of Japan’s most beloved landscapes, a vast, calm, sheltered sea enclosed by Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu and studded with hundreds of green islands large and small. Long a highway of trade and culture, its serene beauty — gentle water, layered island silhouettes, fishing boats and famous sunsets — has inspired poets, artists and travellers for centuries. Kagawa sits right on its shore, and the seascape shapes everything: the ferries fanning out to the islands, the great bridges (like the Seto Ohashi) leaping across it, the island communities and the art destinations of Naoshima and beyond.

item.title: Washuzan Hill: The Seto Ohashi Bridge Viewpoint — Guide
item.description: Washuzan is a modest hill of just 133 metres on the southern coast of Kurashiki, but its view is one of the finest in western Japan. From its granite outcrops the whole eastern Seto Inland Sea opens out below: dozens of green islands scattered across the water, ships threading between them, and the vast Seto Ohashi bridge striding across the strait to Shikoku on a series of enormous suspension spans. It is celebrated as one of Japan’s great sunset spots, when the sea turns gold and the bridge is silhouetted, and later the bridge itself is illuminated.

item.title: Furofushi Onsen: Aomori's Seaside Sunset Bath — Guide
item.description: Furofushi Onsen is a famed seaside hot spring in Fukaura where you soak in amber-coloured open-air baths at the very edge of the Sea of Japan, facing the sunset. Iron-rich water turns golden-brown on contact with the air, and waves break just metres away — a bucket-list bathing experience on the Gono Line coast. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Fukaura, Aomori Hours Day bathing ~8:00–16:00 (varies) Admission Day bath ~¥600 Time needed 1–1.

item.title: Senjojiki Coast: Aomori's Sunset Rock Shelf — Guide
item.description: The Senjojiki Coast at Fukaura is a broad, flat shelf of pale volcanic rock, thrust up from the sea by an earthquake in 1792. A celebrated stop on the scenic Gono Line, it’s known for spectacular Sea of Japan sunsets and easy shoreline strolling over the tabletop rocks. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Fukaura, Aomori Hours Always open (sunset best) Admission Free Time needed About 1 hour Best time Summer & autumn; sunset any clear day What to See The wide flat rock shelf uplifted in 1792.

item.title: Enoshima Guide: Shrine, Sea Candle & Sunset (Kanagawa)
item.description: A small sacred island linked to the Shonan coast by a bridge, Enoshima is one of the most beloved escapes near Tokyo — a hill of shrines, caves, gardens and sea views topped by a lighthouse-like observation tower. Climb (or ride the outdoor escalators) past the Enoshima Shrine to the Sea Candle, whose deck delivers superb panoramas over Sagami Bay to Mt. Fuji, gorgeous at sunset. Below, the wave-carved Iwaya caves and a lively lane of seafood and grilled-octopus stalls make it a perfect half-day, easily paired with the Shonan beaches.

item.title: Umeda Sky Building Guide: The Floating Garden Observatory
item.description: One of Osaka’s boldest pieces of architecture, the Umeda Sky Building is two 40-storey towers joined at the top by a doughnut-shaped Floating Garden Observatory seemingly suspended in mid-air. Glass escalators cross the open void between the towers to reach the rooftop, where an open-air deck gives a 360-degree panorama over the whole of Osaka — spectacular at sunset and after dark. Frequently listed among the world’s great buildings, it’s the city’s best skyline viewpoint and an experience in itself.
